turns.prompt_text: what is the melting point of steel
turns.response_html: The melting point of steel generally ranges from 1370°C to 1540°C (2500°F to 2800°F). The exact temperature depends on the specific alloy composition, as elements like carbon, nickel, and chromium lower the melting point compared to pure iron.

turns.prompt_text: hey Google what is spot welding
turns.response_html:
Spot welding is a resistance welding process used to join overlapping metal sheets by applying pressure and high electrical current to a localized area. The resistance to the current generates heat, melting the metal into a small "nugget" that fuses the pieces together.

How It Works

  • Electrodes: Two copper alloy electrodes pinch the metal sheets together.
  • Heat: A high current passes through the electrodes, heating the contact point.
  • Fusion: The metal melts and cools rapidly, forming a permanent bond without the need for filler material.

This method is standard in automotive manufacturing and sheet metal fabrication because it is fast, easily automated, and efficient for thin materials.
